nodes.label: R5: Errors re-serialised faithfully
nodes.rationale: A Connected-mode failure and a Simulated one must read identically in the response panel — that symmetry is what makes Simulated mode trustworthy.

nodes.label: B1: consoleAuth-only admin operations
nodes.rationale: API keys stay server-only, never in a browser; agency toggling its own plan flags would be self-granting features (D-096).

nodes.label: Node walkthrough — pnpm simulate, 57 steps
nodes.rationale: Steps 21 and 47 block rather than fail because both need a consoleAuth-only action (registering a webhook endpoint, flipping an entitlement flag) this repo has no credential to cross; a blocked run still exits non-zero.

nodes.label: R2: SDK entry points stay separate at module-graph level
nodes.norm_label: r2: sdk entry points stay separate at module-graph level
nodes.rationale: kaafil-js/client must have no code path that imports the API-key branch even by accident; enforced structurally, not by convention.

nodes.label: closing-day-unbuilt (CLOSED 2026-08-16, Phase 14)
nodes.rationale: unlockCloseout is apiKeyAuth only by design — the person who locks a trip is not the person allowed to reopen it.

nodes.label: no-offline-outbox (CLOSED 2026-08-16, Phase 15)
nodes.rationale: A 409 never auto-merges by design; an absent pull section writes nothing, never treated as an empty list.

nodes.label: sync-push-share-unauthenticated (P0, engine-side)
nodes.rationale: POST /api/v1/sync/push/share declares no security scheme at all; CredentialResolver correctly reads that as public, so kaafil-js refuses the call locally rather than sending a traveller's queued forms unauthenticated. Fix is engine-side: declare shareAuth on the route.

nodes.label: Repo gates: typecheck, test, build, simulate
nodes.norm_label: repo gates: typecheck, test, build, simulate

nodes.label: allowBuilds esbuild allowlist
nodes.rationale: pnpm does not run a dependency's build scripts unless allowlisted; esbuild's postinstall puts its platform binary in place, and both tsx and vite are unusable without it — the failure otherwise shows as a confusing missing-binary error on first run.

nodes.label: GAPS.md upkeep obligation
nodes.rationale: A register that lists a shipped capability as missing is worse than no register, because it is read as current.

nodes.label: B9: agency settings endpoints are consoleAuth
nodes.norm_label: b9: agency settings endpoints are consoleauth
nodes.rationale: getAgencySettings/patchAgencySettings now exist but as consoleAuth — the same human-in-the-loop shape as B1, moved from §3 gap to §2 boundary; architecture/14-configuration.md §5 is the doc that is wrong.

nodes.label: comms-email-has-no-address (unscheduled)
nodes.rationale: Neither Traveller nor Manager carries an email column, so every EMAIL send falls through the channel-fallback walk as permanently unconfigured; reported rather than schema-patched to avoid unstated scope creep.

nodes.label: comms-entirely-ungated (unscheduled)
nodes.rationale: engagement-comms RULES R13 says comms is always-available, but the flag catalog is a closed 19-key set with no comms key — the gating it promises is unimplementable as written; opening that table is a commercial decision.

nodes.label: comms-no-production-sender (partly closed 2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: The provider-credential vault shipped (createCommsProviderCredential seals a BYO key server-side); which adapters KAAFIL_SEND resolves outside dev is not observable from the vendored contract, so that half remains unverified.

nodes.label: Why the API key lives here, and only here
nodes.norm_label: why the api key lives here, and only here
nodes.rationale: A key baked into client JavaScript is a key anyone opening devtools now holds; the browser half only ever holds a manager-session token pair minted by this server.
nodes.source_location: Why the API key lives here, and only here

nodes.label: R1: API key read only in backend/server.ts
nodes.norm_label: r1: api key read only in backend/server.ts
nodes.rationale: A partner API key baked into a browser bundle is a key anyone opening devtools now holds; no browser file may import it, receive it as a prop, or accept it from a query string.

nodes.label: POST /sdk — why it exists, and why it is not a pattern to copy
nodes.norm_label: post /sdk — why it exists, and why it is not a pattern to copy
nodes.rationale: Building a 'call anything on my partner-key client by name' RPC gateway would turn a server-only secret into something a browser can indirectly puppet.

nodes.label: POST /sdk allowlisted generic dispatcher
nodes.rationale: This is not a pattern to copy into a real integration — a production backend calls kaafil methods directly with its own validation, not through one generic reflective RPC surface.

nodes.label: R3: Simulated mode needs nothing running
nodes.norm_label: r3: simulated mode needs nothing running
nodes.rationale: Every screen must be backed by browser/src/logic/sim/; a change that makes any Simulated screen require a network call is wrong — this is the repo's best feature.

nodes.label: Simulated mode (no engine, no key, no network)
nodes.norm_label: simulated mode (no engine, no key, no network)

nodes.label: R6: Manager lane goes direct tab-to-engine
nodes.norm_label: r6: manager lane goes direct tab-to-engine
nodes.rationale: This is the real shape of a manager's device; do not interpose a proxy a real deployment would not have.

nodes.label: Connected mode (real HTTP against a real engine)
nodes.norm_label: connected mode (real http against a real engine)
nodes.rationale: The manager-session lane is called directly from the browser tab to the engine on purpose — that's the real shape of a manager's device in production; the playground doesn't interpose a proxy a real deployment wouldn't have.

nodes.label: R7: kaafil-js pinned exact version
nodes.rationale: A floating ^0.1.0-beta.x range is how this repo would silently break on a beta bump; only move to caret once kaafil-js cuts a stable release.

nodes.label: npm dist-tag wrinkle: latest stuck on beta.0
nodes.norm_label: npm dist-tag wrinkle: latest stuck on beta.0
nodes.rationale: npm always assigns the latest tag on a first-ever publish regardless of --tag; every publish since moved only the beta tag, so an unqualified npm install kaafil-js installs the older, buggier version.

nodes.label: The 'raw' badge is gone
nodes.rationale: kaafil-js@0.1.0-beta.3 wired all sixteen resource groups into the browser entry, so no operation this playground drives is unreachable by the SDK any more; a dead badge in a legend reads as a live one.

nodes.label: History of the deleted 'raw' badge
nodes.rationale: raw existed to say 'the endpoint is live, the SDK just cannot reach it' — collapsing 'no SDK path' into 'no path' was a mistake this repo made once and corrected in writing.

nodes.label: agency-admin-upsert-no-sdk-method (CLOSED 2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: The raw-REST workaround this row documented is now a rule violation per CLAUDE.md R4, not a workaround.

nodes.label: dsar-erasure-export-unbuilt (CLOSED 2026-08-20)
nodes.rationale: Erasure anonymizes in place and is idempotent on erasedAt; export is generated fresh on every call, never a cached snapshot.

nodes.label: B2: no POST /api/v1/agencies
nodes.rationale: A platform-minted Agency would fight the CRM's own record on sourceUpdatedAt under last-writer-wins; the CRM's first trip/traveller push creates the Agency instead.

nodes.label: B3: platformAdminAuth-only partner bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Kaafil's own ops team provisioning a new customer is a different actor entirely, not something a partner self-serves.

nodes.label: B4: reviews and support tickets deferred (D-025)
nodes.norm_label: b4: reviews and support tickets deferred (d-025)
nodes.rationale: For v1 a post-trip complaint is the CRM's to handle — a deliberate hand-off, not a gap nobody noticed (D-025).

nodes.label: B5: KaafilClient holds tokens in memory only
nodes.norm_label: b5: kaafilclient holds tokens in memory only
nodes.rationale: A half-durable store is worse than an absent one; the host app is expected to own persistence.

nodes.label: B6: no auth.revoke() method
nodes.rationale: The vendored spec's Auth tag has no revoke operation to wrap; the internal doc listing one is stale against the contract.

nodes.label: B7: no apiKeyAuth trip-listing operation
nodes.rationale: A CRM tracks its own trip refs via externalTripId rather than asking Kaafil to enumerate them back.

nodes.label: B8: no operation reads/lists a Manager entity
nodes.norm_label: b8: no operation reads/lists a manager entity
nodes.rationale: A CRM already holds the externalManagerId it upserted with; there is no server-side directory to page through.

nodes.label: usage-ingest-log-doc-mismatch (P1, doc gap)
nodes.rationale: readUsage/readIngestLog are security: [consoleAuth] in the shipped contract, contradicting architecture/13-operations.md §4.2's claim of API-key auth — the doc is the thing that is wrong.

nodes.label: The ?since= delta cursor must be the server's own clock
nodes.norm_label: the ?since= delta cursor must be the server's own clock
nodes.rationale: The engine's delta window is updatedAt >= since - 5s, deliberately at-least-once; a literal > since silently loses rows to clock skew and millisecond truncation.
